title: MPC-Pipe: an Efficient Pipeline Scheme for Semi-honest MPC Machine Learning
problem: MPC protocols suffer from substantial performance penalties compared to plaintext execution, particularly when applied to ML algorithms due to added computation and communication overhead. Most MPC protocols today sequentially perform communication and computation, requiring computation on shares first and then data communication before proceeding to the next step.
motivation: Efficient secure multi-party computation for ML applications is critical for practical deployment of privacy-preserving ML systems.
method: MPC-Pipe overlaps computation and communication steps rather than doing them one after another—while data is being computed at one machine, it's simultaneously being sent to other machines, keeping both processing and network active. This pipelined approach is applied to both CNNs (convolutional networks for image processing) and Transformers (models for language tasks), eliminating idle time where the system would otherwise wait between stages.
key_novelty: MPC-Pipe overlaps computation and communication steps in encrypted multi-party machine learning so data flows continuously instead of waiting between stages.
contributions: Demonstrates that serialization of computation and communication is unnecessary in MPC for ML
Proposes MPC-Pipe, a pipelined execution scheme that overlaps computation and communication stages
Shows applicability to both CNN and Transformer-based models
Achieves performance improvements over sequential MPC approaches

metrics.speedup: improved performance over sequential MPC baseline

primary_theme: MPC protocol optimization for ML via computation-communication pipelining
